headlines.summary: It's another upvote for an energy source that just a few years ago seemed to be moving toward obsolescence.

headlines.title: Is Constellation Energy (CEG) Above Fair Value After New Nuclear Deals?
headlines.summary: Constellation Energy has delivered a very strong 3 year share price run, yet the recent pullback and fresh long term power deals raise a simple question for investors: Is the current valuation of Constellation Energy stock still grounded in the cash flows the business is expected to generate? The share price has gained about 157% over 3 years, which puts real pressure on the question of whether the current market value is aligned with the cash that can flow out of the business over time.

headlines.title: Constellation's $4.3 Billion Google-Backed Upgrades vs. Vistra's $4.2 Billion Government Loan: Which Nuclear Plan Is Better for Shareholders?
headlines.summary: A different means to the same end gives interested investors something to think about, although this difference doesn't necessarily make one stock a better bet than the other.

headlines.title: What Could Lift Constellation Energy Stock?
headlines.summary: Constellation Energy (CEG) stock has lost 20% over the past twelve months, trailing the S&P 500 and its 17% return. Yet recent business developments present a stark contrast to that market decline. On October 6, 2026, Google agreed to buy nuclear power from Constellation for 20 years, arriving just days after Amazon signed a similar deal. For investors who held the stock through its recent drop, these technology partnerships may look like a turning point.

headlines.title: Stocktwits Power Watch: CEG Bags Google Deal, VST Secures Government Funding, Utility Merger Draws Fire
headlines.summary: U.S. power and utility companies saw major developments last week as rising AI-driven electricity demand fueled new investments, while concerns over consumer costs and regulatory scrutiny complicated consolidation efforts in the sector.

description: Constellation Energy Corporation produces and sells energy products and services in the United States. The company operates through five segments: Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, New York, ERCOT, and Other Power Regions. It offers electricity, natural gas, energy-related products, and sustainable solutions. The company has approximately 31,676 megawatts of generating capacity consisting of nuclear, wind, solar, natural gas, and hydroelectric assets. It serves distribution utilities, municipalities, cooperatives, and commercial, industrial, public sector, and residential customers. The company was incorporated in 2021 and is headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland.
